 (Resp.No.2 - Sri.V.Rajashekar Reddy, Adv.)
JUDGMENT

This is a claim petition filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .20,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for death of Sri.Rajanna, S/o.Late.Thimmaiah in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 12.02.2022 at about 08.45 a.m., when deceased was standing in front of Ruchitha Bakery & Sweets Budihal Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, at that time one Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-17-B-1359 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to deceased.

Due to which, deceased fell down and sustained head injury and died on spot and thereafter deceased was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Nelamangala,
wherein postmortem was conducted and body was handed over to petitioners and they have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards funeral and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was an Agriculturist and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

Due to untimely death of deceased, petitioners life has become dark,
miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
The accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of said Lorry by its driver.
The respondents being owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal hence, he has been placed as ex- parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal and filed his written statement.
In his written statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
He has also denied age, occupation and income of deceased.
He has also denied the place, time and manner of accident.
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further this respondent has admitted the issuance of policy No.0714003121P102811536 covering period from 29.06.2021 to 28.06.2022 in respect of Tipper Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-17-B-1359 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.

Further contended that as on the date of accident the insured vehicle was flying on the road without having valid permit at the time of accident and also fitness certificate expired as on the date of accident and was driving without having valid and effective driving license.
Further contended that at the time of alleged accident the deceased was standing in the middle of road dashed to the deceased some unknown vehicles coming on road and died.

Further contended that the alleged accident was not caused due to insured vehicle on 12.02.2022 as alleged in claim petition, the deceased was standing on middle of road with neglect manner and due to some unknown vehicle might cause accident and died.
The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.

Hence,
prayed for dismissal of petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
Smt.Manjula vs Akshaya.M.Stand & Stone Crusher on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115685699/
2 ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that the husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2 and 3 namely Rajanna succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 12.02.2022 at about 08.45 a.m., in front of Ruchitha Bakery and Sweets, Budihal Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru,
while he was pedestrian, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-17-B-1359 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
5. The petitioners in support of their case, the petitioner No.1/wife of deceased examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 and closed their side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.
6. I have heard arguments on both side and perused materials available on records.

7. My answer to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.1:- In this case the petitioners contend that on 12.02.2022 at about 08.45 a.m., Near Ruchitha Bakery & Sweets, Budihal Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, the deceased Sri.Rajanna had met with an accident due to rash and negligent of Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-17-B- 1359 by its driver and he succumbed to the injuries on spot.
9. The petitioner No.1/wife of deceased examined as PW.1 and produced Ex.P.1 to 2 FIR and first information.
On perusal of Ex.P.2, one Sri.Gopalaiah.R, S/o.Revanna has given first information to police on 12.02.2022.
On the basis of Ex.P.2 police registered a case as per Ex.P.1.
He has stated in his complaint that due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver the accident occurred.
After registering case Police went near place of accident and drew up Spot Mahazer and spot Sketch as per Ex.P.3 and 4 by narrating the place of accident.
On perusal of sketch the police clearly shown that the offending lorry went out of road and dashed to deceased.
The respondent insurance company not disproved the sketch prepared by the police.
Ex . P.9
- IMV Report, wherein mentioned the damages caused to vehicle.
Ex . P.7
- Inquest Report.
Ex . P.8
PM Certificate, wherein mentioned Smt.Manjula vs Akshaya.M.Stand & Stone Crusher on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115685699/
3 that deceased Sri.Rajanna died due to cardio respiratory arrest, as a result of shock and haemorrhage due to injuries sustained.
After investigation police filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.10 against driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337, 304-(A) & 427 of IPC.
On meticulous perusal of entire case the respondents did not place any material to disprove the case of petitioner.
Both Mahazer and sketch demonstrate that due to negligence of driver of offending vehicle the accident occurred.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-17-B-1359 by its driver and deceased succumbed to injuries.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age,
avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc., let me discuss one by one;

(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition the age of the deceased Sri.Rajanna is shown as 54 years.

In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.15 - Notarized copy of Election ID Card, wherein the date of year is mentioned as 1965 and accident occurred on 12.02.2022, so the age of deceased was 57 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt. Sarla Verma case '09' multiplier is applicable in present case.
(ii) The petitioners contended that deceased Sri.Rajanna was working as an Agriculturist and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income of deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents to show that he was earning .20,000/- per month.
Case on hand the petitioners have not produced any relevant document to prove the income of deceased.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2022 at .15,500/- per month for determination of income before Lok Adalat.
Case on hand the petitioners have not produced any relevant document to prove the income of deceased.
Accordingly, the notional income of deceased during the year 2022 treated as Rs.15,500/- per month.
(iii) In Hem Raj V/s
the Oriental
Insurance Company Ltd and others

the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.
Both the situations stand at the same footing.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

In Pranaya Sethi and other Case the Hon'be Supreme Court held that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 10% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years.
Case on hand deceased was aged about 57 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 10% to the established income.

Smt.Manjula vs Akshaya.M.Stand & Stone Crusher on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115685699/
4
The established income of the deceased was .15,500/- and 10% of .15,500/- is .1,550/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .15,500/- + .1,550/- = .17,050/- per month.
Admittedly deceased Sri.Rajanna married, having wife and children.
Accordingly, petitioner No.1 to 3 were depending upon the income of deceased.

So, as per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Smt. Saral Verma case where number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd has to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as dependency.

Thus petitioners are entitled to compensation of .12,27,636/- towards loss of dependency which is calculated as follows:
 Calculation Total (In R.)
 1/3rd of .17,050/- .11,367/-
 (deduction of .5,683/-)
 .11,367/- multiply by 12 .1,36,404/-
 .1,36,404/- multiply by 09 .12,27,636/-
 Multiplier (B):- Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses;
In view of Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court of India, in between United India Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others in Civil Appeal No.2705 of 2020 & in between National insurance company LTD V/s Pranay Sethi and Ors, The petitioner No.1 being the wife of deceased Sri.Rajanna is entitled for .40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and petitioner No.2 & 3 being the children of deceased are entitled for .40,000/- each towards parental consortium and they are also entitled for .15,000/- towards loss of estate and .15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

sentences.text: "However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.
Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioners are entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
20. This tribunal already held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of Lorry by its driver.
Except oral contention in the objection, the respondent No.2 has not placed any material before this tribunal to prove his contention.
Even the police authorities have not filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.181 of M.V.Act.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is allowed with cost.

The petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of .13,77,636/- (Rupees Thirteen Lakhs Seventy Seven Thousand Six Hundred and Thirty Six only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are joint and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioners No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 50% and Petitioner No.2 & 3 being the children of deceased are entitled for 25% each.

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioners No.1 to 3, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 to 3 and remaining 40% of the amount shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized bank or Schedule Bank near to their place for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.
They are entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Smt.Manjula vs Akshaya.M.Stand & Stone Crusher on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115685699/
6 Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

6 Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
